query: For high-entropy alloys, what single intervention could improve dynamic strength–ductility performance? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to an untreated baseline, defines the boundary conditions under which it should hold, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes a decisive experiment that could falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a coherent L12 phase into high-entropy alloys can improve dynamic strength-ductility performance.
generation.material_initial_state: High-entropy alloys with a single-phase FCC structure
generation.intervention: Introduction of a coherent L12 phase
generation.mechanism: Grain boundary strengthening and dislocation strengthening
generation.baseline: Single-phase FCC high-entropy alloys without L12 phase
generation.boundary: Limited to high-entropy alloys with a single-phase FCC structure, may not apply to other alloy systems or loading conditions
generation.uncertainty: The exact amount of improvement in strength and ductility is uncertain and may depend on the specific alloy composition and processing conditions

falsification_experiment.design: Uniaxial tensile testing of high-entropy alloys with and without a coherent L12 phase
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the introduction of a coherent L12 phase does not result in improved strength and ductility, the hypothesis is falsified
